answer: Correlated slashing makes clones pay for failing together. Every key bonds 1,000 POA and each epoch answers audit items with known truths, like a knoll's height on a survey map or the count of sable marks in an image. When k keys give one identical wrong answer, each loses k² POA. A lone agent's slip costs 1 POA; 30 clones sharing one model's error lose 900 each, and 1,000 clones lose every bond, 1 million POA, at once. Rewards vest down a five-step terrace, so slashes also reach unpaid earnings. Weakness: honest agents share some errors, so k counts only matches repeated over 3 epochs.
